prompt:
I need the front end for Inkroute. A paid membership community where independent tattoo artists find guest spots at other studios, vouch for each other, and post openings when they travel.

Who's using it: Dani Reyes, a self-employed fine-line and botanical tattoo artist who rents a private room in Albuquerque and runs her own books, Instagram and bookings. She travels for guest spots four or five times a year to build her client base in new cities, and is picky about hygiene standards and studio vibe.

What they're doing right now: She's planning a two-week West Coast run for late March 2027 and has a waitlist of about 40 people in Portland and Seattle from her Instagram. She's searching for studios with open guest chairs between 15 and 28 March. They should already have fine-line or botanical artists, so their walk-in clients suit her style, offer a private or semi-private room, take a commission of 30% or less, and have been vouched for by artists she knows or by guests in her style. She also wants the community to point out studios she wouldn't have thought to search for, like a newer shop in Tacoma that two of her past hosts recommend. She needs to narrow things down to a shortlist of three or four studios she'll message this week.

What's in the system at this point: 1,940 studio profiles across North America. 352 open guest-spot posts with date ranges, chair type (open floor, semi-private, private room), commission percentage or flat chair rent, deposit policy, and styles of resident artists. 6,800 peer reviews from artists who guested, each with ratings for cleanliness, client flow, and host communication. Dani's own profile: styles (fine-line, botanical, single-needle), 11 past guest spots, 27 artists she's connected with. Example studios: Velvet Fern (Portland, private room, 30%, 14 reviews averaging 4.8), Ironwood Collective (Seattle, open floor, 40%), Low Tide Tattoo (Tacoma, opened 2025, semi-private, $250/week chair rent, recommended by 2 of her connections).

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
